problem: Radiologists dictate reports with software that the founders say has not changed in over a decade; RadMate generates and proofreads the report while they read images.
business_model: B2B SaaS per radiologist (assumed from product; no pricing sourced)

founders.name: Mohamed Khalifa
education: Cornell University (computer science, per YC launch post)
founders.background_notes: Source: YC company page and launch post.

founders.name: Adam Skrocki
founders.background_notes: Source: YC company page and launch post; he cites his father as a radiologist.

competitors.name: Rad AI
competitors.what: Generates the impression section of radiology reports with machine learning
competitors.traction_then: Claimed radiologists save about 20% of CT interpretation time; launch coverage is from 2019
competitors.funding_then: $4M seed in 2019 led by Gradient Ventures (later rounds exist but are not dated in sources opened)

technical_complexity.rationale: Generating full radiology reports from images needs a medical imaging foundation model plus dictation workflow integration, hard for two founders.

defensibility.rationale: No proprietary data or integrations are described and a funded rival already sold similar report tools.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Rad AI already sold report tools before the batch; what happened to RadMate is not public.

market_need_then: Radiology reporting is a repetitive workflow and the company claims 30% fewer words dictated; no independent demand evidence was found.

branding.domain_note: radmate.ai lapsed around August 2025 per a directory, and fetching it redirected to an unrelated domain, which was not followed.

brand_strength.rationale: No source describes the logo, visual style or voice, so the brand cannot be rated above forgettable.

outcome_analysis: RadMate AI was a two person team of Cornell graduates building a radiology reporting copilot, which joined YC in Winter 2024. The YC directory lists it as Inactive and its domain appears to have lapsed in 2025, but no shutdown announcement or post-mortem was found, so the cause is not public. Only a database-reported $500K note is known. No failure factors are assigned because no source states one.
notes: radmate.ai redirected to an unrelated domain (not followed). Funding rests on CB Insights alone (YC standard deal recorded as other); CB Insights calls the company Alive while YC says Inactive. Competitor list limited to one dated source; other directories list RADPAIR and Smart Reporting without dates.
